intent: Turn the provisioned device owner into an actually-enforcing install: block YouTube (a FLAG_SYSTEM package the sweep could not previously touch), and make the enforcer impossible to uninstall while it is enforcing. Done inside the 0-account window, where a mistake costs a re-provision rather than a factory reset.
scope: Non-goal: home coordinate delivery, which needs an in-app writer (run-as is dead on a release build)
changes: DevicePolicyBridge gained setSelfUninstallBlocked/isSelfUninstallBlocked. Device owner already hides Settings' uninstall button, but `adb uninstall` worked without this -- and that path strands ownership with no holder, making a factory reset the only exit.
releaseDeviceOwner now unblocks uninstall BEFORE clearDeviceOwnerApp. Reversed, the block would outlive the ownership that is required to lift it: an app that owns nothing and cannot be removed.

EnforcementRunner.apply re-asserts the block every pass, tracking decision.isEnforcing. Self-healing rather than set-once, and going away from home lifts it -- the app stays removable exactly when enforcement is already off.

pl.infakt.infakt added to config.sh (both the day and night allowlists) and the asset regenerated. It was absent because config.sh describes the rooted phone; the first pass would have hidden it, stranding the SMS-paired banking re-authentication chain.

verification.command: jq allowed_packages vs `pm list packages -3`, comm -23, before applying anything
verification.evidence: Computed the hide set on the PC first. Caught pl.infakt.infakt in it. Confirmed org.fossify.messages, org.fossify.phone, keepass, mbank, revolut, mobywatel and Signal were all allowed -- hiding the SMS app would have stranded every bank re-pairing ahead.

verification.command: adb install -r app-release.apk over the provisioned device owner
verification.evidence: Success, and dumpsys still reported Device Owner Type: 0 with the same admin. This is what the release signing config bought: an in-place update that does not disturb ownership.
'applied LOCATION_UNKNOWN: hid 27, restored 0'. dumpsys: youtube, youtube.music, chrome, vending, videos all hidden=true. Before the FLAG_SYSTEM fix these were invisible to the sweep.

verification.command: dumpsys on the apps that must keep working
verification.evidence: phone, messages, keepass, mbank, revolut, infakt, mobywatel, focus_owner, settings, signal all hidden=false. The phone remains usable and the restore chain is intact.

Failure [DELETE_FAILED_DEVICE_POLICY_MANAGER]; logcat 'setUninstallBlocked(true) -> true'; package still installed. dumpsys device_policy lists PackagePolicyKey{packageUninstallBlocked, com.kuhy.focus_owner}.

After reboot: youtube/chrome/vending still hidden=true, Device Owner Type: 0, uninstall still refused. This is the exact failure that defeated `pm suspend` and `pm disable-user` on this device -- both were cleared by a reboot. Device owner holds.
Kotlin unit tests BUILD SUCCESSFUL. All pre-commit hooks pass, including shfmt/shellcheck on the new restore_apps.sh.

risks: Enforcement is currently PERMANENT, not geofenced. No home_location.json exists, so every pass decides LOCATION_UNKNOWN and fails closed. That is the safe direction, but it means YouTube is blocked everywhere, not only at home.

The geofence cannot be provisioned by the existing push_home_location.sh: it relies on `run-as`, which returns 'package not debuggable' on the release build device owner requires. The fix is an in-app 'set home to current location' action, deliberately NOT an exported intent -- an exported set-home is a bypass, since spoofing home to elsewhere would leave the device permanently 'away' with enforcement off. Deferred: it is an APK update, and updates install in place on the same signature, so it does not need the 0-account window.
com.celzero.bravedns (RethinkDNS) is in the hide set, so enforcement hides the independent DNS-level blocking layer. Not dangerous, but the layers are not additive while enforcing.
com.android.vending is hidden, so no app can be installed or updated from Play while enforcing. Intended -- it is what stops a one-tap YouTube reinstall -- but it is a large blast radius.

The uninstall block is tied to decision.isEnforcing. If a future change makes a pass decide AWAY incorrectly, the block lifts. That is the fail-safe direction (removable rather than stranded), but it is not a hard guarantee.
rollback: In-app 'Release device owner' unblocks uninstall and clears ownership, verified working on this device before any account existed.

IMPORTANT: once a Google account is added, `dpm set-device-owner` can never run again without another factory reset, so releasing becomes one-way. Verify the release path is REACHABLE (device owner: yes, button rendered) rather than pressing it.
To lift enforcement without releasing ownership: add the package to the allowlist in config.sh, regenerate the asset, rebuild, install in place, run a pass.
